paragraphs: Rav Mari son of Rav Pinchas, son of Rav Chisda.

Hyman places him in Rav Ashi’s time. Bava Kamma 117a relates that a man coerced by gentiles pointed out the wine of Rav Mari son of R’ Pinchas son of R’ Chisda. He came before Rav Ashi, who exempted him from liability [supplied פטרינהו, plural]. R’ Abbahu [Hyman says it SHOULD READ R’ Abba] objected to Rav Ashi, etc. Hyman infers from Tosafot on Bava Batra 141a, under lididi, that their Bava Kamma 117a text read “Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, sons of R-H [ר״ה].” But Hyman says our reading is MORE CORRECT: Rav Chisda did IN TRUTH have two sons, Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, but they lived in Rava’s time, as in Kiddushin 32b. This Rav Pinchas had a son named Rav Mari, who did IN TRUTH live in Rav Ashi’s time.

notes.text: The property is wine, and Rav Ashi exempts the coerced man from liability. Hyman’s Tosafot-based variant prints R-H, although his subsequent argument names Chisda; that discrepancy is not silently harmonized.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman argues our reading is MORECORRECT and INTRUTH had two sons in Rava’s time and a later grandson in RavAshi’s time; retain his assertion strength while attributing the genealogy and chronology. No family tree or identities are admitted. Supplied ר״ה in the Tosafot variant remains literal R-H; Chisda is an intended contextual possibility, not verified ה-to-ח letter repair based on another entry. The initial abbreviated Pinchas/Chisda occurrences remain safe R-prime names, while every explicitly full רב in the heading, variant and argument remains Rav. Abbahu and Hyman’s SHOULDREAD Abba have only abbreviated titles and remain R-prime. אחמרא is WINE in this account, not donkeys; RavAshi exempts the coerced informer from liability. The source’s פטרינהו plural differs from the contextual singular liability reading and remains an unresolved literal grammatical detail, not a proved transcription repair.

In the consulted Bava Kamma 117a the man points out the wine and, under the same coercion, carries it with the men. Rav Ashi exempts him in the singular (פטריניה), whereas Hyman prints the plural פטרינהו. The rabbis raise an initial question and Rabbi Abbahu raises the later objection. In the consulted Tosafot on Bava Batra 141a, under lididi, the wording is “Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas, sons of ר״ח.” Hyman prints ר״ה when reporting Tosafot. Kiddushin 32b names Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas at Rava’s son’s wedding and explicitly calls Pinchas a son of Rav Chisda. Ketubot 61a alternatively identifies the two unnamed pious men as Mari and Pinchas, sons of Rav Chisda. Hyman’s proposed reconstruction of the generations draws these notices together.
